member.name: T:Vhi.ControlHandSkeleton
member.summary:
The "control" hand - the ground-truth / cued hand on the left of the scene.
Drives 16 finger joints in one of three modes selected by :
Movement (default): plays a named predefined movement through the state machine waiting → closing → holding → opening → resting, and listens for ←/→/↑/↓ keyboard input to cycle/start/stop. Movement poses come from the TOML loaded via ; the available set is filtered by (AI vs Classifier).
Stream: ignores the state machine and follows a continuous 9-DOF pose streamed in over the MyoGestic_ControlPose LSL inlet (consumed via ).
Idle: resets to the neutral pose and holds it; ignores keyboard, stream, and commands.
Frame-by-frame animation logic runs in _Process; the resulting pose is published to the VHI_Control LSL outlet in _PhysicsProcess. Commands originate from the gRPC (via the public command API on this class) and from local keyboard input - the same methods are called either way.

member.name: T:Vhi.LSLCommunicationController
member.summary:
All Lab Streaming Layer I/O for VHI - the only node that touches LSL directly (and even then only through , never SharpLSL).
Resolves two inlets and publishes two outlets:
Inlet MyoGestic_Output - 9 × float32, drives the predicted hand. Typically ~32 Hz.
Inlet MyoGestic_ControlPose (optional) - 9 × float32, drives the control hand only when its is Stream.
Outlet VHI_Control - the control hand's current pose, 60 Hz. MyoGestic consumes this as a training-target source.
Outlet VHI_Predict - the predicted hand's current pose, 60 Hz. For monitoring / recording alongside EMG.
Stream resolution blocks ~1 s so it runs on a background Task.Run thread; results and log lines are marshalled back to Godot's main thread via CallDeferred. Sample pulls themselves are non-blocking and happen in _Process. Streams are resolved by name only, so a stream with a different type or channel count won't be rejected - just yields wrong motion.

member.name: T:Vhi.PredictedHandSkeleton
member.summary:
The "predicted" hand - the model-output hand on the right of the scene.
Pulls 9-DOF samples from the MyoGestic_Output LSL inlet (via ) each frame and writes per-joint rotations across the same 16-joint subskeleton the control hand uses. When is on, the pose is spherically interpolated (Slerp) toward the new sample at instead of snapping - smoother on the eye, but with a small latency cost.
The "right hand" appearance is achieved by a mirrored root transform on the node; both this node and the control hand instance the same left-hand FBX. The current pose is published to the VHI_Predict LSL outlet at 60 Hz.
